t: You're looking at Camberwell Public Baths, a public leisure centre in Southwark. It opened in 1892 and has run continuously ever since, first as publicly funded community baths and more recently as a leisure centre. Two architects are credited with designing it: Henry Spalding and Alfred Cross. Cross lived from 1858 to 1932, and Spalding from 1838 to 1910. Beyond that, the material I have doesn't say more about their work here, but the building itself is the story: more than a century of Londoners still using it for the same everyday purpose.
